'''Andrew David Hamilton''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 3 November 1952) is a British-American<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hamilton |first1=Andrew |title=A Message From NYU President Andrew Hamilton About the Recent Executive Order on Immigration |url=https://www.nyu.edu/about/news-publications/news/2017/january/a-message-from-nyu-president-andrew-hamilton-about-the-recent-ex.html |website=New York University |publisher=New York University |access-date=7 August 2020 |archive-date=3 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210503181926/http://www.nyu.edu/about/news-publications/news/2017/january/a-message-from-nyu-president-andrew-hamilton-about-the-recent-ex.html |url-status=live }}</ref> [[chemist]] and [[Academic administration|academic administrator]] who served as the 16th president of [[New York University]] from 2016 to 2023. He previously served as vice chancellor of the [[University of Oxford]] from 2009 to 2015 and [[Provost (education)|provost]] of [[Yale University]] from 2004 to 2008.

==Early life and education==
Andrew Hamilton was born on 3 November 1952 in [[Guildford, Surrey]], where he attended [[Royal Grammar School, Guildford|Royal Grammar School]].<ref name="Guardian - Profile" /><ref name="h041">{{cite web | title=Professor Andy Hamilton OG 1971 | website=Royal Grammar School | date=28 June 2022 | url=https://www.rgsg.co.uk/staff/professor-andy-hamilton-og-1971/ | access-date=9 August 2024}}</ref>

Hamilton received a [[first class honours|first class]] [[Bachelor of Science]] with a major in chemistry from the [[University of Exeter]] in the United Kingdom in 1974, a [[Master of Science]] from the [[University of British Columbia]] in Canada in 1976, and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] from the [[University of Cambridge]] ([[St John's College, Cambridge|St John's College]]) in 1980.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew D. Hamilton |url=https://as.nyu.edu/faculty/andrew-hamilton.html |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=as.nyu.edu |language=en-US |archive-date=8 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210508200655/https://as.nyu.edu/faculty/andrew-hamilton.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Guardian - Profile">{{cite news |last1=Topping |first1=Alexandra |date=6 June 2008 |title=Profile: Professor Andrew Hamilton |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/theguardian/2008/jun/06/highereducation |access-date=20 January 2015 |archive-date=20 January 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120193016/http://www.theguardian.com/theguardian/2008/jun/06/highereducation |url-status=live }}</ref>

He was a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[Université Louis Pasteur]] in [[Strasbourg]], France in 1981.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url= http://www.europaeum.org/europaeum/?q=node%2F923|title= Professor Andrew Hamilton|publisher= The Europaeum|access-date= 10 November 2010|archive-date= 14 August 2011|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110814074812/http://www.europaeum.org/europaeum/?q=node%2F923|url-status= live}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1981, he was appointed assistant professor of chemistry at [[Princeton University]] then in 1988 as professor of chemistry at the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. In 1997 he moved to Yale as Benjamin Silliman Professor of [[Chemistry]] and professor of [[molecular biophysics]] and [[biochemistry]] at [[Yale University]]. Hamilton's research has spanned porphyrin, supramolecular, medicinal, bioorganic chemistry and chemical biology. His laboratory is most noted for the design of barbiturate hosts, farnesyl transferase inhibitors, protein surface binders, and helix mimetics.<ref>{{cite web | title=Andrew D. Hamilton | work=Department of Chemistry – Yale University | url=http://www.chem.yale.edu/faculty/hamilton.html | access-date=26 October 2006 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061030145018/http://www.chem.yale.edu/faculty/hamilton.html | archive-date=30 October 2006 | url-status=dead | df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Estroff | first1 = L. A. | last2 = Hamilton | first2 = A. D. | doi = 10.1021/cr0302049 | title = Water Gelation by Small Organic Molecules | journal = Chemical Reviews | volume = 104 | issue = 3 | pages = 1201–1218 | year = 2004 | pmid =  15008620}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Macrocyclic and Supramolecular Chemistry|last1=Knipe|first1=Peter C.|last2=Thompson|first2=Sam|last3=Hamilton|first3=Andrew D.|date=2016-08-08|publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Ltd|isbn=9781119053859|location=Chichester, UK|pages=146–164|language=en|doi=10.1002/9781119053859.ch7|url = http://eu.wiley.com/WileyCDA/WileyTitle/productCd-1119053846.html}}</ref> In 2004 he was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]].<ref name="auto"/>

He also served as [[Provost (education)|provost]] of Yale University from October 2004 to October 2008 after his predecessor, [[Susan Hockfield]], was appointed the 16th president of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. He had previously served as Deputy Provost for Science and Technology for one year under Hockfield, and as chairman of the department of chemistry at Yale.<ref>{{cite web |url = http://ursula.chem.yale.edu/~hamgrp/body1.html |title = Andrew D. Hamilton, Ph.D. |access-date = 22 January 2022 |archive-date = 23 January 2022 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220123010624/http://ursula.chem.yale.edu/~hamgrp/body1.html |url-status = live }}</ref>

On 3 June 2008, [[University of Oxford|Oxford University]] announced Hamilton's nomination for the post of Vice-Chancellor.  On 16 June, it was confirmed that he would succeed [[John Hood (university administrator)|John Hood]] and assume the post for a period of seven years on 1 October 2009.<ref>{{cite web | title=Declaration of approval of appointment of Vice-Chancellor | date=20 June 2008 | work=Oxford University Gazette | url=http://www.ox.ac.uk/gazette/2007-8/weekly/200608/acts.htm#6Ref | access-date=19 June 2008 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080629075012/http://www.ox.ac.uk/gazette/2007-8/weekly/200608/acts.htm#6Ref | archive-date=29 June 2008 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He is an Honorary Fellow of [[Harris Manchester College]] and [[Wolfson College, Oxford|Wolfson College]] at Oxford.<ref>{{cite news |url = https://www.thetimes.com/uk/education/article/fellows-harris-manchester-college-oxford-6qg79v60h3h |title = Fellows: Harris Manchester College, Oxford |access-date = 22 January 2022 |archive-date = 23 January 2022 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220123012846/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/fellows-harris-manchester-college-oxford-6qg79v60h3h |url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wolfson.ox.ac.uk/person/andrew-hamilton |title=Andrew Hamilton |access-date=22 January 2022 |archive-date=23 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220123010625/https://www.wolfson.ox.ac.uk/person/andrew-hamilton |url-status=live }}</ref>

He received honorary doctorates from the [[University of Surrey]], [[Tsinghua University]], and the [[University of Exeter]], among others.<ref>{{cite web |date= |title=Biography |url=https://www.nyu.edu/about/leadership-university-administration/office-of-the-president/andrew-hamilton-biography.html |access-date=5 April 2021 |work=New York University |publisher= |location=New York |archive-date=11 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210411231739/https://www.nyu.edu/about/leadership-university-administration/office-of-the-president/andrew-hamilton-biography.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

===New York University===
On 18 March 2015, [[New York University]] announced Hamilton's appointment to begin as the 16th President of the university. His duties began in January 2016.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://nyulocal.com/on-campus/2015/03/18/oxford-university-administrator-named-next-nyu-president/| title=Oxford University Administrator Named ==Personal life==
Hamilton lives in a university-provided penthouse in [[Greenwich Village]] with his wife Jennifer. He has three children.
